title: Condensed tame-inertia cohomology of finite-field representations with norm-topological coefficients
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p,\ell$, a field $k$ of characteristic $p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended norm topology. Fix a finite intermediate field $\mathbf Q_\ell\subseteq E\subseteq\Omega$. For $F=E$ or $\Omega$, let $C_F(S)=C(S,F)$ on profinite sets, using all continuous maps [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring]; put $C_{F,T}=p_T^*C_F$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use internal modules [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and their ordinary unbounded derived categories and direct images [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull].

For a nonnegative integer $r$, let
$$G=(\prod_{q\ne p}\mathbf Z_q)^r=H\times\mathbf Z_\ell^r,\qquad H=(\prod_{q\ne p,\ell}\mathbf Z_q)^r,$$
with the product profinite topology; $q$ ranges over primes and $\mathbf Z_q=\varprojlim_n\mathbf Z/q^n\mathbf Z$. Fix the standard generators $\gamma_i$ of the $\mathbf Z_\ell$ factors. Let $M$ be a finite-dimensional norm-topological $E$-vector space with a continuous $E$-linear $G$-action $\rho$. Suppose $Q=\rho(H)$ is finite of order prime to $\ell$. Put $N=M^H=\operatorname{im}(e)$ where $e=|Q|^{-1}\sum_{h\in Q}h$. For $F=E,\Omega$, let $M_F$ be the condensed $C_F$-module $S\mapsto C(S,F\otimes_E M)$, with the finite-dimensional product norm topology on $F\otimes_E M$ and the extended $G$-action; define $N_F$ in the same way from $N$. The category of $G$-equivariant condensed $C_F$-modules means module objects equipped with a $C_F$-linear action of the condensed group $S\mapsto C(S,G)$. Write $R\Gamma_G$ for the ordinary total right derived functor of invariants from this abelian category to condensed $C_F$-modules.

Define a cochain complex $K_F(M)$ in degrees $0,\ldots,r$ by
$$K_F(M)^a=\bigoplus_{|I|=a}N_F,\qquad (dx)_J=\sum_{i\in J}(-1)^{\#\{j\in J:j<i\}}(\rho(\gamma_i)-1)x_{J\setminus\{i\}}.$$
Then there is a natural isomorphism $\kappa_F:K_F(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_G(M_F)$ in the ordinary derived category of condensed $C_F$-modules. The isomorphisms are compatible with the degree-zero inclusion of invariants. For the continuous inclusion $E\to\Omega$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], the map $R\Gamma_G(M_E)\to\operatorname{Res}_{C_E\to C_\Omega}R\Gamma_G(M_\Omega)$ induced by $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ corresponds, under $\kappa_E,\kappa_\Omega$, to the termwise inclusion $K_E(M)\to\operatorname{Res}K_\Omega(M)$. If $r=0$, these identifications are the identity $M_F[0]$. Neither a completion nor a union of finite-subextension coefficient sheaves is used.

proof.text: Put $L=\mathbf Z_\ell^r$ and $Q=\rho(H)$. The finite sum $e=|Q|^{-1}\sum_{h\in Q}h$ is a continuous $E$-linear idempotent: multiplication by any element of $Q$ permutes its summands, and $ev=v$ for a $Q$-fixed vector. Thus $\operatorname{im}e=M^H=N$. Each $\rho(\gamma_i)$ commutes with $e$ because the $H$ and $L$ actions commute. Hence $N$ is a finite-dimensional continuous $L$-representation. Choose an $E$-basis of $N$ and extend it by a basis of $\ker e$; in these coordinates $e=\operatorname{diag}(1,0)$. Over both $F$ the same matrix acts on continuous functions. Its image is exactly $N_F$, and its fixed vectors under $H$ are the same image. This verifies the coefficient objects to be used in the reduction, without an infinite average.

source.place: Paragraph (3), tame-boundary local calculation: analytic condensed tame-inertia input; agent proof step 1

proof.text: Every finite quotient of $H=(\prod_{q\ne p,\ell}\mathbf Z_q)^r$ has order prime to $\ell$: its open kernel contains a basic product neighbourhood, leaving finitely many finite $q$-power factors, all with $q\ne\ell$. Apply the prime-to-ell reduction with $B=H$, $L=\mathbf Z_\ell^r$ and $V=M$. The finite-image and prime-to-ell hypotheses are precisely those of the item. It gives the inflation isomorphism $a_F:R\Gamma_L(N_F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_G(M_F)$. This step invokes the analytic reduction for the actual internal condensed modules; the finite sum in step 1 alone does not prove the vanishing of higher $H$-invariants.

source.place: Paragraph (3), tame-boundary local calculation: analytic condensed tame-inertia input; agent proof step 2

proof.text: Apply dense-lattice restriction to the representation $V=N$ from step 1, with $D=\mathbf Z^r$ and the coordinate homomorphism $\iota:D\to L$. It gives $b_F:R\Gamma_L(N_F)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_D(\operatorname{Res}_\iota N_F)$. All coefficients here still consist of all continuous norm-topological functions. The input is a derived-category isomorphism, so no inference from isomorphisms of separate cohomology groups is needed.

source.place: Paragraph (3), tame-boundary local calculation: analytic condensed tame-inertia input; agent proof step 3

proof.text: Use the discrete-lattice Koszul resolution with $R=C_F$, $P=\operatorname{Res}_\iota N_F$, and $T_i=\rho(\gamma_i)|_{N_F}$. These are commuting automorphisms by the product-group action. Its complex is literally $K_F(M)$: label each exterior basis vector by its increasing subset $I$. Removing the $i$th element of $J$ has position $1+\#\{j\in J:j<i\}$, giving exactly the displayed sign. In $d^2$ each unordered pair $\{i,j\}$ occurs twice with opposite signs; the two operators commute, so they cancel. Thus the lattice input provides $\lambda_F:K_F(M)\xrightarrow{\sim}R\Gamma_D(\operatorname{Res}_\iota N_F)$ with the required convention, not just its cohomology.

source.place: Paragraph (3), tame-boundary local calculation: analytic condensed tame-inertia input; agent proof step 4

proof.text: Define $\kappa_F=a_F\circ b_F^{-1}\circ\lambda_F$ in the derived category. All three factors are invertible by steps 2--4, so this is an isomorphism of the required direction. Naturality follows by composing the naturality squares of those three maps and inverting the square for $b_F$. On invariant elements, $\lambda_F$ is their inclusion in degree zero, $b_F$ is the identity under the invariant identification, and $a_F$ is induced by $N_F\hookrightarrow M_F$. Therefore this composite is compatible with the prescribed degree-zero inclusion.

source.place: Paragraph (3), tame-boundary local calculation: analytic condensed tame-inertia input; agent proof step 5

proof.text: Write $u_A,u_B,u_C$ for the coefficient maps on $R\Gamma_G(M_F)$, $R\Gamma_L(N_F)$ and $R\Gamma_D(\operatorname{Res}_\iota N_F)$, and $u_K$ for the termwise coefficient inclusion. The coefficient clauses of the three inputs give $u_Aa_E=(\operatorname{Res}a_\Omega)u_B$, $u_Cb_E=(\operatorname{Res}b_\Omega)u_B$, and $u_C\lambda_E=(\operatorname{Res}\lambda_\Omega)u_K$. Multiplying the middle equality by the inverses of $b_E$ and $\operatorname{Res}b_\Omega$ gives $u_Bb_E^{-1}=(\operatorname{Res}b_\Omega)^{-1}u_C$. Substitute into the first and third equalities to obtain $u_A\kappa_E=(\operatorname{Res}\kappa_\Omega)u_K$. The map $u_K$ is literally $x_I\mapsto1\otimes x_I$, since every differential matrix is over $E$. This is exactly the requested coefficient comparison.

source.place: Paragraph (3), tame-boundary local calculation: analytic condensed tame-inertia input; agent proof step 6

proof.text: If $r=0$, then $H=L=D=1$, $Q=1$, $e=1$ and $N=M$. The reduction for trivial $B$, the rank-zero lattice restriction, and the rank-zero Koszul identification are identities by their stated normalizations. The definition of $\kappa_F$ is consequently the identity $M_F[0]$. If $M=0$, or if $N=0$, the same construction gives the zero complex and the unique corresponding isomorphism. No step changes to completed coefficients or to a union of finite-subextension coefficient sheaves.
